svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "CRISPR-Cas9: a tool for editing genes at a chosen site."], [1, "A guide RNA, designed to match the target sequence, is loaded into Cas9."], [3.5, "Cas9 scans the DNA and stops at a PAM next to the matching sequence."], [6, "The DNA is unwound and the guide RNA base-pairs with the target strand."], [8.5, "Cas9 cuts both strands: a double-strand break."], [11, "The cell repairs the break. Without a template, bases are often inserted or deleted: the gene is knocked out."], [14.5, "With a template DNA, the cell can copy in a precise change."]]
svg.title: CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing
svg.desc: Cas9 loaded with a guide RNA finds a target next to a PAM, unwinds the DNA, the guide pairs with the target strand, Cas9 cuts both strands, and the break is repaired by end joining (knock-out) or with a template (precise edit).
svg.text: Short example sequence; a real guide is about 20 bases.

g.data-info: A nuclease from bacteria (part of their immune defence against viruses). It cuts both DNA strands.
The gene to be edited. The target is a 20-base sequence next to a PAM (NGG) that Cas9 recognises.
A short sequence (5′-NGG-3′) next to the target. Cas9 only cuts where a PAM is present.
About 20 bases complementary to the target, attached to a scaffold that binds Cas9: it takes Cas9 to the exact site.
Cas9 cuts both strands about 3 base pairs before the PAM.
Non-homologous end joining often inserts or deletes bases, disrupting (knocking out) the gene. If a template is supplied, homology-directed repair copies it in: a precise edit.

g.text: bases inserted or deleted at the cut → frameshift
the cell copies a supplied DNA template
→ precise change, e.g. correcting a mutation
